abstract: Exercise-induced temporal responses in serum components, such as extracellular vesicles (EVs), remain incompletely characterised. Here, serum was collected from healthy, physically active participants (n=20; 10 males, 10 females) before and at 3-minutes, 1-hour and 2-hours after a 30-minute cycle ergometer bout performed at 70% of maximal oxygen uptake. EVs were characterised by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis and mass spectrometry; serum cytokines were quantified in parallel. The main effect of time on EV concentration and size was not significant. However, there was a transient decrease in EV size at 1-hour in both sexes. Averaged across post-exercise time points, males had smaller EVs and higher levels of 99 EV cargo proteins and of soluble regulators Tie-2, VCAM-1, Eotaxin and CRP. Platelet-associated EV proteins decreased from 1-hour post-exercise in both sexes and, in the pooled cohort, correlated temporally with vascular and inflammatory cytokines and blood cell counts. Partial least squares analysis indicated that baseline adiposity and fitness influenced EV size shifts mostly in males. Of 518 EV proteins, 19 showed nominally significant sex differences in their response trajectory to exercise. Post-hoc comparisons at 2-hours post exercise identified also several between-sex differences in EV protein cargo, all higher in males. VEGF-D was the only cytokine showing a nominal sex-divergent response. This study indicates that acute vigorous exercise does not change the concentration of EVs but elicits a change in their size, particularly in men, while there is also a sex-divergence in response to exercise in EV cargo proteins.

metadata.title: Serum responses to acute vigorous intensity exercise: vesicle analysis with an omics approach

summary: Acute vigorous cycling changed serum extracellular vesicle size, not number, with sex-divergent EV protein cargo and platelet-EV responses in 20 healthy adults.
title: Serum responses to acute vigorous intensity exercise: vesicle analysis with an omics approach
